Photograph: Henry Nicholls/PA Andy Burnham Analysis Burnham’s visit to Kyiv marks a renewal of badly needed support for Ukraine Luke Harding and Dan Sabbagh in Pavlohrad, Ukraine As well as pledging military help and diplomatic backing, the prime minister could be useful in dealing with the US Mon 24 Aug 2026 12.33 EDT Last modified on Mon 24 Aug 2026 12.42 EDT Share Since moving into Downing Street in July, Andy Burnham – a foreign policy neophyte – has expressed strong support for Ukraine. But on Monday he saw the bitter human cost of the war up close for the first time, visiting Kyiv during his first international trip as prime minister. The occasion was the 35th anniversary of Ukraine’s independence. Volodymyr Zelenskyy gave awards to the families of fallen soldiers. Relatives wept, hugging Ukraine’s president. Photos of young men in their prime were shown on a giant screen. The setting was St Sophia cathedral in the old heart of the Ukrainian capital. Built in the 11th century, the building predates Moscow and is a symbol of Ukraine’s ancient statehood. Next to it were modern weapons used by Kyiv in its struggle against Russia including quadcopter drones and unmanned land robots. In a speech in front of other western leaders, Burnham compared Ukraine’s fight to that waged by Britain during the darkest days of the second world war. “My nation kept the flame of European freedom alive in the 20th century, you hold that flame in the 21st,” he declared. Like other high-profile visitors, Burnham arrived with a gift. Since 2023 the UK and France has been providing Kyiv with long-range Storm Shadow or Scalp (as the French version is known) cruise missiles, used to knock out Russian naval ships and command centres. Burnham hands secret missile technology to Ukraine – The Latest Read more It was now handing over British blueprints for key components, Burnham said, so Ukraine could eventually make its own version with France. More Storm Shadows could go some way to dealing with Ukraine’s biggest problem – the wave of ballistic missiles fired by Russia that rain down on Kyiv and other cities most nights. As of now, Ukraine has run out of US-made Patriotic interceptors capable of shooting them down. The Trump administration is disinclined to provide more. Civilians killed by Russia in Ukraine The British cruise missiles carry a larger payload than the long-range drones favoured by Kyiv. They could be used to destroy enemy ballistic missile launch systems, which can be quickly moved, and are dotted around sites in western Russia. Depending on their range, they could also disable military runways and aerodromes. But nobody expects production to start soon. In the meantime, the Kremlin has responded with characteristic belligerence. Vladimir Putin’s press spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, said Moscow would destroy any Ukrainian Storm Shadow factories, and accused London of taking part in the war and adding “fuel to the fire” though it is France that is helping with building them. Last week Russia threatened “consequences” over the supply of British drones to Kyiv and withdrew its ambassador from London . It is unclear how Putin might escalate further. He has already sent assassins to poison Russian dissidents on UK territory including the murder in 2006 of Alexander Litvinenko, killed with radioactive tea. Burnham appears unmoved by what he dubbed “outrageous” Russian threats, an encouraging sign for Kyiv. On Monday he pointed out that it was Putin who “started the fire” with his illegal and unprovoked invasion, and assured Zelenskyy of his “personal commitment” to Kyiv’s existential cause. Ukraine has warmly welcomed the Storm Shadow initiative. Oleksandr Merezhko, head of the Ukrainian parliament’s foreign affairs committee, told the Guardian he hoped manufacture could begin in “months, not years”. “We have proved many times we can do impossible things in producing weaponry,” he said, saying the missile “strengthened” Kyiv’s position in negotiations with Moscow. Of Burnham’s visit, he added: “For us, it’s hugely symbolic and important. It illustrates that for the UK Ukraine remains a top priority. You are an important bridge and have rectified the situation whenever we have a crisis in our relations with the US. Your king is a valuable diplomatic tool and puts in a good word for us with Trump.” The trip also signals to allies that the UK will continue to play a leading role in the coalition of the willing after the departure of Keir Starmer. Co-hosting a coalition meeting for the first time, Burnham said Europe would do everything it could to source more Patriotic interceptors for Ukraine. Zelenskyy has asked for 300 to help the country survive the coming winter. Burnham’s speech made clear that he regards Ukraine’s struggle as Britain’s too – at a time when the US has effectively given up on its attempts to broker a peace deal, and has halted direct military aid. “Ukraine has been Europe’s protector, not a drain on our security but the frontline in keeping Europe safe,” he added. “The Ukrainian people deserve not just our continued support but our gratitude and respect,” he said. Ukrainian leaders and soldiers are grateful for British diplomatic and moral support, though they know that London’s military power is limited. Storm Shadow is deemed to have been one of the UK’s most useful contributions but stockpiles were modest. Ukraine’s focus has been on developing its own long-range drones and cruise missiles, such as Fire Point’s Flamingo, which have been used to strike refineries and warehouses deep inside Russia. The goal is to attack Russia with 1,000 drones and some missiles a day this year, not when Storm Shadow production lines are ready. But the deal that Burnham has agreed with Zelenskyy is an important renewal of goodwill. At some point Zelenskyy will probably need the help of European allies whenever the White House re-engages with the peace process. Burnham may become an important interlocutor with Trump, and today’s trip is from Ukraine’s perspective an encouraging start. Betrayal by Luke Harding (Guardian Faber, £20) is published on Thursday. CREDIT: Pedro Gomes/Getty Images Twenty One Pilots have asked fans attending their upcoming All Points East gig to help chronicle the experience. READ MORE: Twenty One Pilots live at Mad Cool: alt-rock innovators play their hearts out The Grammy Award -winning duo are set to make their debut at London’s Victoria Park on Sunday August 30. It will be their only UK concert of the year, and will see them supported by Wunderhorse , Nova Twins and more – you can find any remaining tickets here . Advertisement Ahead of the gig, their creative and content director, Mark C. Eshleman, sent out a request to fans attending, inviting them to be a part of capturing footage from the night. Taking to Instagram, he told fans they would be releasing footage at a later date, but wanted “to add something unique to toss in between a few of the songs during the edit. “I am on the hunt for about 10 fans that I can send both Hi-8 and miniDV cameras to capture a little of their fan life as well as the journey to the show,” he wrote. WATCH “It will feel vlog-style but your footage doesn’t have to be very wordy. I am mostly interested in capturing what it feels like to be a fan. You can show off some artwork, what your themed bedroom looks like, an outfit you are making for the show.” Auditions closed yesterday (August 15), and producers will collect cameras and footage when gig-goers arrive on the festival grounds later this month. View this post on Instagram Recommended Earlier this year, Twenty One Pilots released a concert film, More Than We Ever Imagined , capturing a Mexico City gig on their ‘The Clancy World Tour’, which saw them perform to 65,000 people. Joseph and Dun provided commentary throughout the film, reflecting on their journey to the career milestone. Back in July, they performed a headline set at Mad Cool in Madrid, which NME described as a “show that anyone can appreciate” , and more recently, brought their current festival run to Budapest, following stops across Europe. NME’s Rhian Daly went along to their set at Sziget Festival , and described it as “the latest in a long line of theatrical performances, with fireworks and pyrotechnics glittering across the stage. “As if that wasn’t enough to mark the set as a spectacular, Twenty One Pilots roped in a famous face to really seal the deal. “I’m Jack White and I give Tyler and Josh permission to do this,” The White Stripes frontman said in a pre-recorded video message that illuminated the big screens. The “this” in question? I expected bad times to arrive with ideological revolutions, some religion old or novel, or due to ecological disaster. Not race! Now, as race riots and race-flash-mob-violence sweeps the US, 138 thousand Germans (according to Destatis) escaped Germany in 2015 in order to get away from the dismal public safety situation and dark future prospects, as well as the banning of relevant speech and the rampant extrajudicial prosecutions that are catalyzed by the internet’s social networks – they work just like the old witch hunts, modern mob violence that destroys careers and families without the victims being able to even point to specific perpetrators. Especially high IQ sub-populations are targeted. This is natural, because intelligent people are usually those who have something relevant to say. Moreover, especially Whites and White males as well as Jews are targeted, which thus samples the sub-populations with the highest IQs. Since the intelligent flee, one speaks commonly of ‘brain-drain’. The average IQ in Germany declined by four points (from 102 down to 98) over the last decade (2003 to 2013). That is 0.4 points per year. It needs only 4 to 5 years until it falls below 96, the threshold between rather lawful civilized society and widespread corruption. What is the brain-drain’s contribution to this decay? Germany has 82 million people. 138 thousand Germans left, the same as if every German above IQ 142 had left. (You can check that yourself: Paste"=82175700*(NORMDIST(200,98,15,TRUE)-NORMDIST(142,98,15,TRUE))" into an Excel spreadsheet formula and hit enter to evaluate. Then start to play, but careful. I did this once and became a racist! Just joking, I have always been a racist . But not kidding – you might end up spending weekends on simulating populations like here or here or here .) There are Germans below 142 IQ that left and as many above 142 stayed, so this is an overestimation of the effect. Nevertheless, this brain-drain would depress the German average IQ by only 0.08 points, far less than the usual 0.4 points per year. (So since that was an overestimation ... do I have to spell it out?) Germany received over a million refugees in 2015. Syria has average IQ 83 and 17 million people. 1.95 million fled Syria, the same as if every Syrian above 101 had left. According to this overestimate of brain-drain, even the least intelligent Syrian refugee is still more intelligent than the average IQ in Germany ! (Doing this for Africa instead of Syria will even increase the IQ further - this has also been discussed differently by John Derbyshire . BTW: This brain-drain would depress Syria’s IQ from 83 down to 79.6; so refugees are a huge problem for the source countries, but the effect on Germany's IQ is tiny, even assuming the refugees are really this intelligent.) This shows that the current batch of immigrants cannot do much in terms of decreasing the average IQ in Germany either. It may do something, but it cannot be a large influence. Quick, progressive science bloggers and other impartial media: Cut these facts out and blow them out of proportion without mentioning the context! Do not read on! Therefore, the IQ decline is almost entirely due to the dysgenic IQ-decline in Germany and the regression of the previous generation’s immigrant’s children toward the racial mean. Without understanding “ regression toward the mean ” one cannot understand the dangers of immigration. The current immigration will accelerate the decay further only in the next generation. The dominant factor is the different birth rates of the sub-populations that are already inside the borders. It is unstoppable even if we were to stop immigration now. Many Germans flee to Eastern Europe, countries such as Hungary, the only EU country democratic enough to ask its citizen whether they desire unlimited mass immigration; the referendum resulted in 92% saying “No Way!” Does the common population understand “regression toward the mean” better than the intellectuals in power? Well, such kind of knowledge is inherent in our evolved decision strategies. So, Let The Donald Trump! (BTW: Information about 'Regression Toward The Mean', for example on Wikipedia, is usually politically correct and thus quite misleading. John Derbyshire's explanation does not stress the causal genetic aspects. Genes are re-shuffled every generation. This swamps the selection of high IQ immigrants. Miscegenation leads to depression to even below the mean (also with "hybrid vigor" in the second generation)!
